To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show that tera­hertz electromagnetic pulses allow for coherent steering of spins across a potential barrier, with characteristic fingerprints in the temporal and spectral domain.

terahertz pulses can switch the spin of a material in a coherent manner, and that this can be detected via a characteristic temporal signature and a spectral fingerprint of the collective spin resonance.

1) terahertz pulses can be shaped to trigger coherent spin dynamics in antiferromagnets; 2) the spin motion is ballistic and can be controlled with an external bias field; 3) coherent switching of the spin is accompanied by unique temporal and spatial fingerprints; 4) the spin motion can be described by an effective spin Hamiltonian.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel concepts for spintronics and quantum information technology.
the control of spin dynamics by intense terahertz fields.
the development of new materials for spintronics applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have demonstrated a coherent spin precession in an antiferromagnet, with the possibility to tune it by a terahertz pulse, with a characteristic time of about one picosecond and with an amplitude that is about 20% of the total moment.
the authors have demonstrated the possibility of switching the spin state of antiferromagnetic material using a terahertz field, and that the spin switching is coherent.
the terahertz pulses are used to switch spins between two states separated by the potential barrier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the terahertz field is able to switch the spins of TmFeO 3 from one potential well to the other one.
we have demonstrated the first coherent spin switching in an insulator with an all-optical approach and that we have observed the fingerprints of this phenomenon.
the terahertz electric fields of the antenna-enhanced terahz pulses can switch spin between two metastable states separated by a barrier, with minimal dissipation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
terahertz pulses can be used as a tool to control spins in antiferro- or ferrimagnets with high precision.
coherent spin switching is not just possible, but that it can be observed in real time.

the terahertz electric fields of subwavelength antennas can be used to coherently steer the spins of antiferromagnets over potential barriers, and that the corresponding spin dynamics can be characterized by unique temporal, spectral and polarization signatures.
